newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds TSB staff vote for half-day strike.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds TSB staff vote for half-day strike.

text.p: Staff at Lloyds TSB Group Plc have voted in favour of a half-day strike on Christmas Eve but a similar group at National Westminster Bank rejected the strike call, banking and finance trades union BIFU said on Tuesday.
BIFU said staff were protesting at the decision of the banks to keep branches open on the afternoon before Christmas when they have "traditionally" closed at midday.
At Lloyds TSB, 65 percent of those who voted were in favour of the stoppage while at NatWest, 54 percent voted against a strike.
Lloyds TSB said it was disappointed by the strike call.
"We believe the figures show that the vast majority of our staff realise the need to be there for our customers when they need us," said a spkeswoman for Lloyds TSB.
BIFU said it balloted around 18,500 staff at Lloyds TSB of which 37 percent voted.

At NatWest, only 22 percent of the 11,700 members balloted voted and BIFU said this was because they had only two days in which to vote given the fact that, by law, the union would have to give the employer one week's notice of any strike action. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717.
